title: Case study: reviewer experience from ADaM metadata
text: usability checks read metadata origin , derived variables, derivation. example ADaM metadata carry yet, trace mapping : direct copy predecessor, anything real derivation rule derived. Joining two gives realistic Define-style table.
code: meta <- adam_metadata  key <- paste(meta$dataset, meta$variable) mk  <- paste(trace_mapping$adam_dataset, trace_mapping$adam_var) idx <- match(key, mk) has <- !is.na(idx) deriv <- trace_mapping$derivation_text[idx]  meta$origin <- "Assigned" meta$origin[has & grepl("Direct copy", deriv)]  <- "Predecessor" meta$origin[has & !grepl("Direct copy", deriv)] <- "Derived" meta$derivation <- NA_character_ meta$derivation[has] <- deriv[has]  head(meta[, c("dataset", "variable", "label", "origin", "derivation")], 6) #> # A tibble: 6 × 5 #>   dataset variable label                     origin      derivation              #>   <chr>   <chr>    <chr>                     <chr>       <chr>                   #> 1 ADSL    STUDYID  Study Identifier          Predecessor Direct copy from DM.ST… #> 2 ADSL    USUBJID  Unique Subject Identifier Predecessor Direct copy from DM.US… #> 3 ADSL    SUBJID   Subject Identifier        Predecessor Direct copy from DM.SU… #> 4 ADSL    SITEID   Study Site Identifier     Predecessor Direct copy from DM.SI… #> 5 ADSL    AGE      Age                       Predecessor Direct copy from DM.AGE #> 6 ADSL    AGEU     Age Units                 Predecessor Direct copy from DM.AG…

title: Usability Indicators with r4subusability
text: R4SUB framework organises submission-readiness evidence four pillars: quality, traceability, risk, usability. Usability measures easy regulatory reviewer understand navigate submission package - dimension six major regulatory authority profiles allocate 15 % 20 % total submission-readiness weight. r4subusability implements four indicators make pillar: Every assessment function returns validated R4SUB evidence table via r4subcore::as_evidence(), output immediately compatible scoring profiling layers.

title: Usability Indicators with r4subusability
text: four indicators driven shared configuration list. defaults reflect common regulatory requirements, can override element: Key parameters: label_min_chars / label_max_chars - acceptable label length window (default: 3-40 characters). required_origins - origins must derivation text ("Derived", "Assigned"). reviewer_guide_keywords - strings identify reviewer guide asset ("ADRG", "SDRG", "reviewers_guide", "reviewer_guide"). weights - relative indicator weights summing 1.
code: cfg <- usability_config_default() str(cfg) #> List of 5 #>  $ label_min_chars        : int 3 #>  $ label_max_chars        : int 40 #>  $ required_origins       : chr [1:2] "Derived" "Assigned" #>  $ reviewer_guide_keywords: chr [1:4] "ADRG" "SDRG" "reviewers_guide" "reviewer_guide" #>  $ weights                :List of 4 #>   ..$ label_quality      : num 0.3 #>   ..$ define_completeness: num 0.35 #>   ..$ annotation_coverage: num 0.25 #>   ..$ reviewer_guide     : num 0.1 cfg$weights #> $label_quality #> [1] 0.3 #>  #> $define_completeness #> [1] 0.35 #>  #> $annotation_coverage #> [1] 0.25 #>  #> $reviewer_guide #> [1] 0.1

title: Usability Indicators with r4subusability
text: assess_label_quality() checks every variable label : Presence - missing empty label fail severity = "high". Minimum length - label shorter label_min_chars warn. Maximum length - label longer label_max_chars warn. Otherwise - pass severity = "info" metric_value = 1.
code: meta_labels <- data.frame(   dataset  = c("ADSL",    "ADSL", "ADAE"),   variable = c("USUBJID", "AGE",  "AETERM"),   label    = c(     "Unique Subject Identifier",  # OK - 26 chars     "Age",                         # OK - 3 chars (at minimum)     ""                             # fail - empty label   ),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  ev_label <- assess_label_quality(meta_labels, ctx) #> ✔ Evidence table created: 3 rows ev_label[, c("location", "result", "severity", "metric_value", "message")] #>       location result severity metric_value                message #> 1 ADSL.USUBJID   pass     info            1      USUBJID: label OK #> 2     ADSL.AGE   pass     info            1          AGE: label OK #> 3  ADAE.AETERM   fail     high            0 AETERM: label is empty

title: Usability Indicators with r4subusability
text: assess_define_completeness() verifies Define-XML metadata populated correctly. variables whose origin required_origins, non-empty derivation text mandatory. USUBJID AETERM come CRF - derivation required, pass. AGE "Derived" derivation text, also passes. variable origin = "Derived" derivation text fail:
code: meta_define <- data.frame(   dataset    = c("ADSL",    "ADSL",   "ADAE"),   variable   = c("USUBJID", "AGE",    "AETERM"),   label      = c(     "Unique Subject Identifier",     "Age",     "Adverse Event Term"   ),   origin     = c("CRF",     "Derived", "CRF"),   derivation = c(NA,        "Derived from BRTHDTC and RFSTDTC", NA),   codelist   = c(NA,        NA,        NA),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  ev_define <- assess_define_completeness(meta_define, ctx) #> ✔ Evidence table created: 3 rows ev_define[, c("location", "result", "severity", "message")] #>       location result severity                          message #> 1 ADSL.USUBJID   pass     info USUBJID: origin 'CRF' documented #> 2     ADSL.AGE   pass     info       AGE: derivation documented #> 3  ADAE.AETERM   pass     info  AETERM: origin 'CRF' documented meta_bad <- data.frame(   dataset    = "ADSL",   variable   = "TRTEDT",   label      = "Treatment End Date",   origin     = "Derived",   derivation = NA_character_,   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) ev_bad <- assess_define_completeness(meta_bad, ctx) #> ✔ Evidence table created: 1 row ev_bad[, c("location", "result", "severity", "message")] #>      location result severity                                         message #> 1 ADSL.TRTEDT   fail     high TRTEDT: derivation missing for origin 'Derived'

title: Usability Indicators with r4subusability
text: assess_annotation_coverage() works dataset level. dataset computes proportion derived variables non-empty derivation text: >= 90 % -> pass 70 - 89 % -> warn < 70 % -> fail ADSL 2 derived variables, 1 annotated -> 50 % -> fail. ADAE derived variables coverage applicable (na).
code: meta_annot <- data.frame(   dataset    = c("ADSL",   "ADSL",   "ADSL",   "ADAE",   "ADAE"),   variable   = c("AGE",    "SEX",    "TRTEDT", "AESTDTC","AEENDTC"),   origin     = c("Derived","CRF",    "Derived","CRF",    "CRF"),   derivation = c(     "Derived from BRTHDTC and RFSTDTC",     NA,                                   # CRF - not counted     NA,                                   # Derived but not documented     NA,                                   # CRF - not counted     NA                                    # CRF - not counted   ),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  ev_annot <- assess_annotation_coverage(meta_annot, ctx) #> ✔ Evidence table created: 2 rows ev_annot[, c("asset_id", "result", "metric_value", "message")] #>   asset_id result metric_value                                        message #> 1     ADSL   fail          0.5 ADSL: 50% of derived variables annotated (1/2) #> 2     ADAE     na          1.0                     ADAE: no derived variables

title: Usability Indicators with r4subusability
text: assess_reviewer_guide() checks character vector asset names keyword matches reviewer_guide_keywords (case-insensitive, matched word boundary "ADRG" matches "adrg.pdf" unrelated substring). returns single evidence row.
code: # Submission package includes an ADRG ev_guide_pass <- assess_reviewer_guide(   assets = c("ADRG", "define.xml", "datasets"),   ctx    = ctx ) #> ✔ Evidence table created: 1 row ev_guide_pass[, c("result", "severity", "message")] #>   result severity                                             message #> 1   pass     info Reviewer guide asset detected in submission package # Submission package is missing a reviewer guide ev_guide_fail <- assess_reviewer_guide(   assets = c("define.xml", "datasets"),   ctx    = ctx ) #> ✔ Evidence table created: 1 row ev_guide_fail[, c("result", "severity", "message")] #>   result severity                                                      message #> 1   fail     high No reviewer guide (ADRG/SDRG) detected in submission package

title: Usability Indicators with r4subusability
text: usability_indicators() runs four assessments single call returns one combined evidence table:
code: meta_full <- data.frame(   dataset    = c("ADSL",    "ADSL",    "ADAE"),   variable   = c("USUBJID", "AGE",     "AETERM"),   label      = c(     "Unique Subject Identifier",     "Age",     "Adverse Event Term"   ),   origin     = c("CRF",     "Derived", "CRF"),   derivation = c(NA, "Derived from BRTHDTC and RFSTDTC", NA),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  assets <- c("ADRG", "define.xml")  ev_all <- usability_indicators(meta_full, assets = assets, ctx = ctx) #> ✔ Evidence table created: 3 rows #> ✔ Evidence table created: 3 rows #> ✔ Evidence table created: 2 rows #> ✔ Evidence table created: 1 row #> ✔ Bound 4 evidence tables: 9 total rows  # One row per variable per indicator, plus one row for the reviewer guide nrow(ev_all) #> [1] 9 table(ev_all$indicator_id, ev_all$result) #>         #>         na pass #>   U-001  0    3 #>   U-002  0    3 #>   U-003  1    1 #>   U-004  0    1

title: Usability Indicators with r4subusability
text: usability_summary() produces structured usability_result object per-indicator pass/fail/warn counts overall score. print method renders colour-coded console report: can also access underlying summary data frame programmatically:
code: res <- usability_summary(ev_all) print(res) #>  #> ── R4SUB Usability Assessment ── #>  #> Study: "STUDY01" | Variables assessed: 3 #>  #> ✓ Variable Label Quality: 100% pass (3/3) #> ✓ Define-XML Completeness: 100% pass (3/3) #> ✓ Annotation Coverage: 100% pass (1/1) #> ✓ Reviewer Guide Presence: 100% pass (1/1) #>  #> ℹ Overall usability score: 100% res$summary[, c("indicator_id", "indicator_name", "n_pass", "n_fail", "pct_pass")] #> # A tibble: 4 × 5 #>   indicator_id indicator_name          n_pass n_fail pct_pass #>   <chr>        <chr>                    <int>  <int>    <dbl> #> 1 U-001        Variable Label Quality       3      0        1 #> 2 U-002        Define-XML Completeness      3      0        1 #> 3 U-003        Annotation Coverage          1      0        1 #> 4 U-004        Reviewer Guide Presence      1      0        1

title: Usability Indicators with r4subusability
text: Override specific defaults without replacing entire list:
code: cfg_strict <- usability_config_default() cfg_strict$label_min_chars <- 5L   # stricter minimum length cfg_strict$label_max_chars <- 30L  # tighter maximum  ev_strict <- assess_label_quality(meta_full, ctx, config = cfg_strict)

title: Usability Indicators with r4subusability
text: evidence table returned r4subusability function plugs directly rest R4SUB pipeline: Evidence can also persisted audit trails:
code: # Downstream - illustrative, requires r4subscore and r4subprofile score  <- r4subscore::compute_score(ev_all) report <- r4subprofile::render_profile(score, authority = "FDA") tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds") r4subcore::export_evidence(ev_all, tmp, format = "rds") ev_reloaded <- r4subcore::import_evidence(tmp, format = "rds")

text: usability_report() orchestrates whole package one call: runs four scored indicators advisory diagnostics single metadata frame assembles tidy per-check summary, one combined findings frame, R4SUB evidence. invents new criteria – overall score exactly weighted usability_summary() score scored indicators, diagnostics contribute descriptive finding counts .

title: Consolidated Usability Report — usability_report
text: Runs every usability check package provides one metadata frame single call assembles results one coherent report. pure orchestration aggregation layer: invents new pass/warn/fail criteria, thresholds, scores. scored indicators keep U-001..U-004 semantics weighted roll-(usability_summary()), advisory diagnostics keep descriptive, unscored finding counts.

title: Consolidated Usability Report — usability_report
code: usability_report(   metadata,   assets = character(0),   ctx,   config = NULL,   diagnostics = TRUE )

title: Consolidated Usability Report — usability_report
text: metadata data frame columns dataset, variable, label, origin, derivation (optional), codelist (optional). May span several datasets (one row per variable per dataset). Compatible adam_metadata, sdtm_metadata, oncology_metadata datasets r4subdata. assets character vector asset names present submission package, passed assess_reviewer_guide(). Defaults character(0). ctx run context created r4subcore::r4sub_run_context(). config configuration list usability_config_default(). NULL default configuration used. diagnostics Logical; TRUE (default) advisory diagnostics run aggregated alongside scored indicators. FALSE scored indicators reported.

title: Consolidated Usability Report — usability_report
text: usability_report object (list class "usability_report") : study_id study identifier evidence. n_datasets Number distinct datasets metadata. n_vars Number variable-level locations assessed (counted usability_summary()). overall_score weighted scored-indicator score usability_summary(); NA nothing applicable. n_fail,n_warn Total fail warn rows across scored indicators. n_findings Total number advisory diagnostic findings. checks tidy per-check summary tibble: one row per check check, check_name, check_type ("scored" "diagnostic"), n_items, n_pass, n_warn, n_fail, n_na, n_findings, pct_pass. Scored-columns NA diagnostics. findings combined tidy tibble offending items across checks, columns check, check_type, finding_type, dataset, variable, detail. evidence combined R4SUB evidence tibble scored indicators (see r4subcore::as_evidence()). scored usability_summary() result scored indicators. config configuration used.

title: Consolidated Usability Report — usability_report
text: Two families check combined: Scored indicators assess_label_quality() (U-001), assess_define_completeness() (U-002), assess_annotation_coverage() (U-003), assess_reviewer_guide() (U-004), run together usability_indicators(). emit validated R4SUB evidence carry pass/warn/fail/na results weighted overall score. Advisory diagnostics label_consistency(), variable_name_conformance() (run distinct variable names), variable_attribute_consistency(). descriptive: report tidy set findings never scored rolled overall score. overall usability score exactly weighted score usability_summary() four scored indicators; diagnostics contribute finding counts, never pass/fail judgement.

title: Consolidated Usability Report — usability_report
code: ctx <- suppressMessages(r4subcore::r4sub_run_context(study_id = "STUDY01")) rep <- suppressMessages(usability_report(   r4subdata::oncology_metadata,   assets = c("ADRG", "define.xml"),   ctx = ctx )) rep$checks #> # A tibble: 7 × 10 #>   check      check_name check_type n_items n_pass n_warn n_fail  n_na n_findings #>   <chr>      <chr>      <chr>        <int>  <int>  <int>  <int> <int>      <int> #> 1 U-001      Variable … scored          32     32      0      0     0          0 #> 2 U-002      Define-XM… scored          32     29      0      3     0          3 #> 3 U-003      Annotatio… scored           3      2      0      1     0          1 #> 4 U-004      Reviewer … scored           1      1      0      0     0          0 #> 5 label_con… Label Con… diagnostic      NA     NA     NA     NA    NA          0 #> 6 variable_… Variable … diagnostic      NA     NA     NA     NA    NA          0 #> 7 variable_… Variable … diagnostic      NA     NA     NA     NA    NA          0 #> # ℹ 1 more variable: pct_pass <dbl> print(rep) #>  #> ── R4SUB Usability Report ── #>  #> Study: "STUDY01" | Datasets: 3 | Variables assessed: 32 #>  #> Scored indicators #> ✓ Variable Label Quality: 100% pass (32/32) #> ✓ Define-XML Completeness: 90.6% pass (29/32) #> ✗ Annotation Coverage: 66.7% pass (2/3) #> ✓ Reviewer Guide Presence: 100% pass (1/1) #>  #> Advisory diagnostics (descriptive, unscored) #> ✓ Label Consistency: no findings #> ✓ Variable Name Conformance: no findings #> ✓ Variable Attribute Consistency: no findings #>  #> ℹ Overall usability score: 88.4%

title: Diagnose Cross-Dataset Variable Attribute Consistency — variable_attribute_consistency
text: Produces descriptive, tidy report variables whose data attributes drift across datasets appear. variable name used one dataset (example USUBJID ADSL ADAE) expected carry data type, storage length, display format everywhere; mismatch common, objective source reviewer friction frequent cause transport-file surprises.

title: Diagnose Cross-Dataset Variable Attribute Consistency — variable_attribute_consistency
code: variable_attribute_consistency(   metadata,   attributes = c("type", "length", "format") )

title: Diagnose Cross-Dataset Variable Attribute Consistency — variable_attribute_consistency
text: metadata data frame least columns dataset (character) variable (character), plus attribute columns named attributes. Compatible adam_metadata, sdtm_metadata, oncology_metadata datasets r4subdata. attributes character vector naming attribute columns check cross-dataset consistency. Defaults c("type", "length", "format"). name present metadata skipped.

title: Diagnose Cross-Dataset Variable Attribute Consistency — variable_attribute_consistency
text: tibble one row per finding columns: finding_type One "inconsistent_type", "inconsistent_length", "inconsistent_format" (one per checked attribute). variable variable whose attribute inconsistent. dataset dataset row reports. attribute name attribute column involved. value attribute value variable carries dataset (character). detail human-readable description finding. every shared variable consistent, zero-row tibble columns returned.

title: Diagnose Cross-Dataset Variable Attribute Consistency — variable_attribute_consistency
text: Like label_consistency() variable_name_conformance(), unlike scored usability indicators (example assess_label_quality()), function score anything emit R4SUB evidence rows; purely advisory diagnostic. result tidy: one row per affected dataset occurrence per attribute, variable differs type length appears two finding types. following finding types may emitted, one per checked attribute column present metadata: inconsistent_type type attribute differs across datasets. inconsistent_length length attribute differs across datasets. inconsistent_format format attribute differs across datasets. attribute columns named attributes actually present metadata checked; requested attributes absent silently skipped, function safe call metadata carries . Values compared trimming leading trailing white space; NA empty-string values treated missing never drive finding, variable simply lacks (say) format one dataset reported.

title: Diagnose Cross-Dataset Variable Attribute Consistency — variable_attribute_consistency
code: meta <- data.frame(   dataset  = c("ADSL", "ADAE", "ADSL", "ADAE"),   variable = c("USUBJID", "USUBJID", "AGE", "AGE"),   type     = c("Char", "Char", "Num", "Char"),   length   = c(20, 40, 8, 8),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) # USUBJID differs in length; AGE differs in type. variable_attribute_consistency(meta) #> # A tibble: 4 × 6 #>   finding_type        variable dataset attribute value detail                    #>   <chr>               <chr>    <chr>   <chr>     <chr> <chr>                     #> 1 inconsistent_length USUBJID  ADAE    length    40    variable 'USUBJID' has 2… #> 2 inconsistent_length USUBJID  ADSL    length    20    variable 'USUBJID' has 2… #> 3 inconsistent_type   AGE      ADAE    type      Char  variable 'AGE' has 2 dis… #> 4 inconsistent_type   AGE      ADSL    type      Num   variable 'AGE' has 2 dis…  # Restrict the check to a single attribute. variable_attribute_consistency(meta, attributes = "type") #> # A tibble: 2 × 6 #>   finding_type      variable dataset attribute value detail                      #>   <chr>             <chr>    <chr>   <chr>     <chr> <chr>                       #> 1 inconsistent_type AGE      ADAE    type      Char  variable 'AGE' has 2 disti… #> 2 inconsistent_type AGE      ADSL    type      Num   variable 'AGE' has 2 disti…

what: Check Variable and Dataset Names Against SAS v5 Transport Constraints — variable_name_conformance
title: Check Variable and Dataset Names Against SAS v5 Transport Constraints — variable_name_conformance
text: Produces descriptive, tidy report names conform SAS Version 5 transport (XPT) format naming constraints still govern many regulatory submissions. default conforming name eight characters long, built upper-case letters, digits, underscore, start digit.

title: Check Variable and Dataset Names Against SAS v5 Transport Constraints — variable_name_conformance
code: variable_name_conformance(   names,   max_length = 8L,   allowed_chars = "A-Z0-9_",   allow_leading_digit = FALSE )

title: Check Variable and Dataset Names Against SAS v5 Transport Constraints — variable_name_conformance
text: names character vector names check, data frame whose column names checked. Anything else coerced .character(). max_length Maximum allowed name length, characters. Defaults 8L, SAS v5 transport limit. allowed_chars regular-expression character-class body describing permitted characters (text appear [ ]). Defaults "-Z0-9_": upper-case letters, digits, underscore. Use, example, "-Za-z0-9_" also permit lower-case letters. allow_leading_digit Logical; FALSE (default) name begins digit reported starts_with_digit.

title: Check Variable and Dataset Names Against SAS v5 Transport Constraints — variable_name_conformance
text: tibble one row per non-conforming name per reason, columns: name non-conforming name. reason One "too_long", "invalid_character", "starts_with_digit", "empty". detail human-readable description finding. every name conforms, zero-row tibble columns returned.

title: Check Variable and Dataset Names Against SAS v5 Transport Constraints — variable_name_conformance
text: Unlike scored usability indicators (example assess_label_quality()), function score anything emit R4SUB evidence rows; purely advisory diagnostic. Every reported name may appear one row breaks one rule, result tidy (one row per name per reason). following reasons emitted: too_long name longer max_length characters. invalid_character name contains least one character outside set described allowed_chars. starts_with_digit first character name digit. Suppressed allow_leading_digit = TRUE. empty name NA, empty, white space . limits configurable function can check naming conventions (example longer SAS V8/V9 limit, case-insensitive character set). defaults encode documented SAS v5 rule.

title: Check Variable and Dataset Names Against SAS v5 Transport Constraints — variable_name_conformance
code: # A character vector of variable names variable_name_conformance(   c("USUBJID", "SUBJECTID", "trt01p", "2VISIT", "AE_TERM") ) #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>   name      reason            detail                                             #>   <chr>     <chr>             <chr>                                              #> 1 2VISIT    starts_with_digit name starts with a digit                           #> 2 SUBJECTID too_long          name has 9 characters; exceeds maximum of 8        #> 3 trt01p    invalid_character name contains characters outside the allowed set …  # Check the column names of a data frame directly df <- data.frame(USUBJID = 1, AgeInYears = 2, check.names = FALSE) variable_name_conformance(df) #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>   name       reason            detail                                            #>   <chr>      <chr>             <chr>                                             #> 1 AgeInYears invalid_character name contains characters outside the allowed set… #> 2 AgeInYears too_long          name has 10 characters; exceeds maximum of 8       # Configurable limits: allow lower case and a longer (V8) limit variable_name_conformance(   c("trt01p", "SUBJECTIDENTIFIER"),   max_length = 32L,   allowed_chars = "A-Za-z0-9_" ) #> # A tibble: 0 × 3 #> # ℹ 3 variables: name <chr>, reason <chr>, detail <chr>

title: r4subusability (development version)
text: Add usability_report(): consolidated rollup runs every usability check package one metadata frame single call assembles results one usability_report object. orchestrates scored indicators (usability_indicators(), U-001..U-004) advisory diagnostics (label_consistency(), variable_name_conformance(), variable_attribute_consistency()), returning tidy per-check summary (pass/warn/fail/na counts finding counts), single combined findings frame offending items, combined R4SUB evidence. invents new criteria: overall score exactly weighted score usability_summary() scored indicators, diagnostics contribute descriptive finding counts . print() method included. Add variable_attribute_consistency(): descriptive diagnostic reports variables whose data attributes (type, length, format) drift across datasets appear. variable name shared several datasets expected carry type, length, format everywhere; mismatches reported tidy tibble, one row per affected dataset per attribute. attributes checked configurable absent columns skipped. purely additive affect existing usability scores. Add variable_name_conformance(): descriptive diagnostic checks variable dataset names SAS v5 transport (XPT) naming constraints (maximum length eight characters; upper-case letters, digits, underscore ; starting digit). limits configurable result tidy tibble non-conforming names reason. purely additive affect existing usability scores. Add label_consistency(): descriptive diagnostic reports duplicate labels within dataset, variable name carrying inconsistent labels across datasets, missing dataset-level (table) labels, tidy tibble. purely additive affect existing usability scores. Fix README quick-start example, called usability_indicators() non-existent study_id argument omitted required run context. Correct usability-indicators vignette: drop stale "ARG" entry documented reviewer_guide_keywords defaults, describe reviewer guide match word-boundary (substring) matching, match code.

title: r4subusability 0.1.0
text: Initial release. usability_config_default(): default configuration usability assessments. assess_label_quality(): check variable label presence length (U-001). assess_define_completeness(): check Define-XML origin derivation fields (U-002). assess_annotation_coverage(): check proportion derived variables annotated (U-003). assess_reviewer_guide(): check reviewer guide presence submission package (U-004). usability_indicators(): run four assessments one call. usability_summary() print.usability_result(): summarise display results.
